minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard tax abatement and overlay risk (427 requests) and an ARPA option for trucks; no substantive votes.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the town manager report a snow and ice overage and a health insurance deficit, then discussed the capital plan and whether ARPA funds could buy DPW trucks and an ambulance. Most of the meeting covered the overlay account, the roughly 427 abatement requests, and a Proposition 2.5 presentation by the chair. The only vote was adjournment; January 26 minutes were deferred.

attendees.role: finance director (referred to; possibly off the call)

public_comment.topic: Corrected his earlier capital plan remarks on DPW trucks: two already ordered and back-ordered, FY24 plan adds two more; noted town manager's reprioritization of items seven through 29 and the overlay backfill from free cash.
Opposed using the pavement management plan line to cover the snow and ice deficit; said ARPA funds should pay for trucks instead.

budget_items.what_was_said: A projected deficit this year from enrollment changes; the town manager and finance director identified surpluses elsewhere to cover it.
Currently over budget mainly from contractor dependence with four of seven trucks out of commission, higher contractor rates and salt costs.
The plan is to cover the snow deficit mainly from this operating line, plus a DPW salary surplus; the line has funds left this year.

budget_items.topic: ARPA for DPW trucks and ambulance
budget_items.what_was_said: The select board suggested using ARPA to buy the trucks and ambulance, which would not free up other cash and would later be repaid via town meeting appropriation.
The capital plan recommends using this fund for large vehicles; changing its purpose or using it to refund ARPA needs a two-thirds town meeting vote.
The overlay budgeted this year was slightly exceeded by what the assessors raised; a deficit must be funded at town meeting or on the recap.
About 427 abatement requests have been filed; a member roughly estimated the total exposure, and the town manager said she will recommend a conservative overlay amount and is reserving free cash.
Requests exceed the ARPA funding available, with some already spent on covid items.
The chair presented revenue shares, with the tax levy about two-thirds of the total.
The rate fell as valuations rose to stay within the levy limit.

what_happened.line: The committee took no substantive votes; the only vote was to adjourn, and approval of the January 26 minutes was deferred because of a correction.
The town manager reported a projected health insurance deficit and a snow and ice overage, to be covered mainly from other lines with surpluses.
The committee discussed whether federal pandemic relief (ARPA) money could buy DPW trucks and an ambulance, to be repaid later by a town meeting appropriation.
The committee reviewed the overlay account and the abatement requests filed, with the town manager planning a conservative overlay recommendation and reserving free cash.
Budget-season meetings with department presentations were scheduled over the following weeks.

why_it_matters: Covering the snow and ice overage from the pavement management line could mean less road work, and the overlay and truck financing choices bear on the tax rate and on what town meeting is asked to vote.
Changing the special purpose stabilization fund's purpose, or using it to repay ARPA, would need a two-thirds vote at town meeting.
